bullets.title: CPI Tomorrow Is the Key Fed Catalyst; September Hike at ~50/50
bullets.body: Market-implied odds of a September rate hike hover around 42–51% per fed funds futures, with zero probability of a cut. Multiple Fed officials (Goolsbee, Venable, Hammack) have flagged inflation as the economy's biggest problem. JPM models July core CPI at +0.22% m/m (3.4% YoY headline); a print above 0.30% risks 1.5–2.5% SPX decline, while 0.20–0.25% supports 25–75bp gain. Options pricing ~0.9% 1-day SPX move. 22V investor survey shows 48% expect inline 0.2% core with risk-on reaction, but 48% believe conditions still need to tighten.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh's Task Forces Signal Potential Policy Framework Overhaul
bullets.body: WSJ's Nick Timiraos reports Warsh's task forces appear designed to build a replacement for the current monetary policy framework, though the existing framework remains operative until a new one is articulated. Multiple Fed officials are seeking evidence inflation can reach 2% without further tightening.

bullets.title: Iran Holds Hormuz Shut; Oil Volatile, EIA Raises Brent Forecast to $87
bullets.body: Iran's security council stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until conditions are met, including a U.S. policy shift and frozen asset release. EIA raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $87/bbl from $82/bbl and cut 2026 global supply estimates by 1.1M bpd to 100.8M bpd. WTI traded near $83 before giving back gains on US-Iran deal hopes. U.S. Energy Secretary Wright reported 7-day average flows near 9M bpd through the strait, and Qatar LNG loadings hit their highest since March.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Edges Lower; Mag 7 Dragged Index; Semis and Energy Lead
bullets.body: S&P 500 closed down ~0.3% with GOOGL (-3.7%), AMZN (-2.1%), and AAPL (-1.1%) the primary drags; without those three, the index would have finished roughly flat. Semis outperformed (+0.9%) led by semi-cap equipment and memory, while Communications Services underperformed (-2.1%). Energy was the top-gaining sector (+1.06%) on oil strength. Mag 7 is trading ~2 standard deviations below its 2018-present forward P/E mean, implying ~30% upside to one standard deviation below mean per JPM.

bullets.title: CTAs Triple Underweight Bonds; $300M/bp Exposure Into CPI
bullets.body: CTA positioning is at extreme short in bonds with a record ~$300M per basis point exposure going into Wednesday's CPI release. Morgan Stanley notes front-month CDX IG at-the-money vol implies ~1.1 bps daily breakeven (15th percentile of 5-year lookback), with clients buying tail vols in Sep-Jan via payer spread structures. Credit vol hedges outperformed equity vol hedges during recent geopolitical turmoil.

bullets.title: 10Y Yields Disconnected from Fed Cuts; Barclays Sees Structural Pressure
bullets.body: The 10-year yield has risen 98 bps since the Fed began cutting rates on September 18, 2024, despite 175 bps of cuts — the only prior analog is the 1980 cycle (119 days). Barclays attributes persistent long-end yield elevation to private investors now holding ~73% of the Treasury market, up from ~50% a decade ago. The 3-year Treasury auction priced at 4.291% (vs. 4.179% prior) with improved bid-cover of 2.71 but declining indirect participation to 64.2%.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI Capex Commitments Hit $2.6T; Systematic Buyers Set to Reload
bullets.body: Hyperscalers have collectively lined up $2.6T in future data center and AI infrastructure spending per Bloomberg. Citadel reports the leverage unwind has largely run its course and systematic strategies are poised to add exposure in NVDA, MU, SNDK, and LITE. JPM notes Mag7/hyperscaler backlogs grew 150% YoY to $1.7T vs. capex growth of 80%.

bullets.title: NVDA's $500B AI Financing Plan Divides Wall Street; Circular Financing Debate
bullets.body: Nvidia unveiled a $500B+ financing partnership with six financial firms (Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, GS, KKR) to fund chip purchases without using Nvidia's balance sheet. The structure has raised circular financing concerns that Jensen Huang publicly addressed. ORCL CDS spreads crossed back above 200 bps, with hyperscaler CDS volumes hitting all-time highs on credit worries. Analyst commentary notes token prices are in freefall from open-weight models, shifting the narrative to compute securitization.

bullets.title: TSMC July Revenue Hits Record; AI Filling Every Wafer Slot; CoWoS Near Capacity
bullets.body: TSMC posted record July revenue as AI demand fills all available wafer capacity. The company is discussing CoWoS advanced packaging constraints at OCP APAC and is close to but not fully meeting customer demand. NVDA is internally modeling that a broad HBM downspec across Rubin GPUs could enable 30–50% more shipments from the same HBM supply, assuming CoWoS and compute-die supply keep pace.

bullets.title: Asia Tech Recovery Broadening Beyond AI; Non-Semis Exports Growing 25% Annualized
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley finds Asia's recovery is broadening beyond AI semiconductors, with non-semis exports at 8-year highs and non-AI capital goods imports in a steady uptrend. Non-AI exports are growing at a 25% annualized pace since October 2025, with the expansion covering China, India, Korea, Taiwan, Australia, and Japan.

bullets.title: VIX Below 15; SPY 773 Call Wall $6.3B; Put IV at Year Lows
bullets.body: VIX fell below 15, last seen before US-Iran tensions began, and remains far below its long-term average. SPY has a $6.3B call wall at 773 and $4B+ positive gamma at 780. One-month 25-delta SPY puts are trading at 14% IV, the lowest since December 2024, despite CPI and PPI catalysts on deck.

bullets.title: US Household Debt Dips to $18.8T; Credit Card Debt Rises to $1.26T; Auto Loans Record
bullets.body: NY Fed Q2 data shows total US household debt fell 0.1% to $18.8T — the first decline since COVID — driven by a $74B drop in mortgage balances. However, credit card balances rose $21B to $1.26T and auto loans hit a record $211B. Subprime auto originations also hit a record, concentrated in 30–50 year-olds. Aggregate delinquency improved modestly to 4.7% in Q2, and student loan newly delinquent balances fell to 7.8%.

bullets.title: ADP Private Hiring Slows Sixth Consecutive Week; Labor Market Stable, Not Strong
bullets.body: ADP weekly private hiring fell to 8,250 jobs vs. 15,000 the prior week, the sixth consecutive weekly deceleration. Fed's Goolsbee characterized the labor market as 'stable but not strong,' with the employment/population ratio in a steep downtrend since June 2024 that failed to recover in July.

bullets.title: Existing Home Sales Miss; Inventory Highest Since 2019
bullets.body: July existing home sales fell 1.7% m/m to 4.06M units, worse than the +1.0% consensus estimate. US housing inventory exceeds 1.1 million units, the highest since 2019. Median home price rose 2% YoY to $434,100, a July record. US rents are down 1.1% YoY for the 38th consecutive month.

bullets.title: Google Gemini Surpasses 1B Monthly Users; 14th Product to Reach Milestone
bullets.body: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced Gemini now has over 1 billion monthly active users, calling it Google's fastest-growing product and its 14th product to cross the 1B milestone. Some skepticism noted on whether the count includes auto-installs.

bullets.title: INTC's $20B Equity Offering 3x+ Oversubscribed; AI Foundry Pivot Underway
bullets.body: Intel priced an upsized $20B share sale that attracted demand 'several times' the available shares, with approximately one-third of order participants receiving nothing. Management framed the raise as supporting the AI foundry business expansion, not distress financing. Unusual $5M+ call options flow was also noted in INTC.

bullets.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism Near 1-Year High; BofA Sees K-Shape Narrowing
bullets.body: NFIB Small Business Optimism rose 2.4 points in July to its highest level since August 2025, beating consensus. BofA consumer data shows the economy becoming less K-shaped with lower-income household spending accelerating relative to upper-income cohorts. Variant Perception's US growth leading indicator also ticked up, pointing to steady economic outlook.

bullets.title: Canada-US Trade Talks Resume; Canada and USTR Greer Meet Tuesday
bullets.body: Canada's trade minister met with USTR Greer Tuesday at 1:30 PM ET as officials plan a potential deal to present to Trump next week per CBC sources. The Canadian dollar and bilateral trade tensions remain a watch item heading into the meeting.

bullets.title: Jefferies Semis Analyst Bullish on AMD, NVDA, AVGO, COHR, LITE, MRVL for AI Cycle
bullets.body: Jefferies semis analyst Blayne Curtis is conducting an NYC roadshow September 2–3 covering post-earnings themes and AI infrastructure outlook. Buy ratings include AMD ($650 PT), NVDA ($300 PT), AVGO ($550 PT), COHR ($375 PT), LITE ($1,200 PT), MRVL ($325 PT), CRDO ($270 PT), ALAB ($450 PT), SNDK ($1,750 PT). INTC and TXN remain at Hold.

bullets.title: S&P 500 2026 EPS Now Expected +32%; Mag7 Backlog +150% YoY to $1.7T
bullets.body: Wall Street has revised S&P 500 2026 EPS growth expectations to +32%, more than double the 15% forecast at year-start. Mag7/hyperscaler contract backlogs grew 150% YoY to $1.7T vs. capex growth of 80%, and net new ARR is also up 150% YoY. JPM's bull case is supported by 2% real GDP trend growth, 50%+ YoY EPS growth, and a disinflationary trajectory.
